title: Data Sources, Databases and Your First SQL Queries

lesson.html:
By the end of Day 4 you should be able to:

  1. Classify data sources as internal or external, and as structured, semi-structured or unstructured.
  2. Explain what a relational database is: tables, rows, columns, primary keys and foreign keys.
  3. Open a database in VS Code with SQLTools and run a query.
  4. Retrieve data with SELECT, FROM and DISTINCT.
  5. Filter rows with WHERE: =, <>, >, <, AND, OR, IN, BETWEEN, LIKE, IS NULL.
  6. Sort and shorten results with ORDER BY and LIMIT.
  7. Save your work as a query script (.sql): our evidence for today. (Integrated: Use information systematically.)

Materials you need today

Item File / Location
SQL lab folder (open this folder in VS Code) Day04/assets/Day04_SQL_Lab/
The database Day04_SQL_Lab/aling_nena.db
Your query script (you type your answers here) Day04_SQL_Lab/Day04_Queries.sql
Demo video (captions, shortcut-key overlays) Day04/demo/Day04_Demo_Your_First_SQL_Queries.mp4

How to use this handout. Every new term has a "Sa simpleng salita" (in simple words) box. Read that first, then the formal definition. The Glossary is on the last page.

lesson.h: Part 1 — Where Does Data Come From? (Data Sources)
lesson.html:
Sa simpleng salita: A data source is the place where data comes from. Aling Nena's cash register is a data source. So is the PAGASA weather forecast, and so is a Facebook comment about her store.

Internal vs external

Type Meaning Aling Nena examples
Internal Data the business creates itself POS sales receipts, inventory list, suki membership list, employee time records
External Data that comes from outside the business PAGASA weather, PSA inflation rates, supplier price lists, Facebook page reviews, GCash settlement reports

Structured, semi-structured, unstructured

Sa simpleng salita: Structured data fits neatly in rows and columns, like a class record. Unstructured data does not: photos, voice messages, long comments. Semi-structured is in between: it has labels, but not a fixed table.

Type Looks like Examples Easy to analyze?
Structured Rows and columns with a fixed format Database tables, Excel sales sheet, CSV file ✅ Yes, directly with SQL or Excel
Semi-structured Labels/tags, but flexible JSON from an app, XML, emails (To/From/Subject + free text) ⚠ After some processing
Unstructured No fixed format Photos of receipts, voice messages, Facebook comments, CCTV video ❌ Needs special tools

Primary vs secondary data. Primary data you collect yourself for your purpose (a customer survey). Secondary data was collected by someone else (PSA census figures).

Use information systematically (Integrated competency)

Before you pull any data, answer four questions and write them down. This is called a data source inventory:

Question Example
What data do I need? Daily sales per branch
Where is it (which source/table)? aling_nena.db, table sales
Who owns it / who do I ask? Aling Nena (store owner), branch managers
How good is it (complete, up to date)? Jan 5 – Mar 29, 2026; 500 sales; walk-in sales have no customer

lesson.h: Part 2 — What Is a Relational Database?
lesson.html:
Sa simpleng salita: A database is an organized cabinet of data. Each table is one drawer that holds one kind of thing: one drawer for branches, one for products, one for customers, one for sales. Relational means the drawers are connected by ID numbers, like a receipt that says "product 107" instead of writing the whole product name again.

Word Meaning Example in aling_nena.db
Table A set of rows and columns about one kind of thing products
Row (record) One item / one event One product: Ligo Sardines 155g
Column (field) One property, the same type for every row unit_price
Primary key (PK) A column whose value is unique for every row; the row's ID product_id (101, 102, …)
Foreign key (FK) A column that points to the primary key of another table sales.product_id → products.product_id
NULL "No value / unknown". Not zero, not blank text sales.customer_id of a walk-in customer
DBMS The software that stores and manages the database SQLite (today), MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQL Server

Why not just one big Excel sheet? If the product name were written on every one of 500 sales, a typo or a price change would have to be fixed 500 times. In a relational database the product is written once in products, and every sale just points to it. Less repetition, fewer errors.

The Aling Nena database: 4 tables

Table Rows Primary key Foreign keys What one row means

products 32 product_id — One product on the shelf
customers 46 customer_id — One suki (member) customer
sales 500 sale_id branch_id, product_id, customer_id One line on a receipt (Jan 5 – Mar 29, 2026)

┌──────────────┐        ┌──────────────────┐          ┌───────────────┐
│ branch_id PK │◄───────│ branch_id   FK   │          │ product_id PK │
│ branch_name  │        │ sale_id     PK   │    ┌────►│ product_name  │
│ city         │        │ sale_date        │    │     │ category      │
│ manager      │        │ sale_time        │    │     │ unit_price    │
│ opened_on    │        │ product_id  FK   │────┘     │ supplier      │
│ floor_area   │        │ customer_id FK   │────┐     └───────────────┘
│ status       │        │ quantity         │    │      customers
└──────────────┘        │ unit_price       │    │     ┌────────────────┐
                        │ total_amount     │    └────►│ customer_id PK │
                        │ payment_method   │          │ first_name ... │
                        └──────────────────┘          └────────────────┘

First 3 rows of sales:

sale_id sale_date sale_time branch_id product_id customer_id quantity unit_price total_amount payment_method

lesson.h: Part 3 — Setting Up: VS Code + SQLTools
lesson.html:
Sa simpleng salita: SQL (say "S-Q-L" or "sequel") is the language we use to ask a database questions. VS Code is the free editor where we type those questions. SQLTools is an add-on (extension) for VS Code that sends our questions to the database and shows the answers as a table.

One-time setup on your PC (the trainer has done this on the lab PCs):

  1. Install Node.js LTS (nodejs.org) and Visual Studio Code (code.visualstudio.com).
  2. In VS Code press Ctrl + Shift + X (Extensions), search SQLTools, click Install. Then search SQLTools SQLite and install it too.
  3. The first time you connect, SQLTools may ask to install sqlite3. Click Install now and wait for "Successfully installed".

Every day: open the lab folder

  1. Copy Day04_SQL_Lab into your DAL3/Day04/ folder.
  2. In VS Code: File → Open Folder… (Ctrl + K, Ctrl + O) → choose Day04_SQL_Lab → Select Folder. If asked "Do you trust the authors?", click Yes, I trust the authors.
  3. In the Explorer on the left, click Day04_Queries.sql.
  4. The connection Aling Nena is already set up (in .vscode/settings.json) and connects by itself. To see it, click the SQLTools icon (a database cylinder) in the left bar. Expand Aling Nena → Tables to see the 4 tables and their columns.

Run a query

  1. Type the query on an empty line. End it with a semicolon ;.
  2. Select (highlight) the query: put the cursor at the end of the query, then press Shift + Home (one line). For a longer query, press Shift + ↑ to select more lines.
  3. Press Ctrl + E, then Ctrl + E again. Or click ▷ Run on active connection just above the query.
  4. The result opens in a panel below. The bottom-right corner says how many rows, e.g. 1-5 of 5.
  5. Press Ctrl + S to save your script often.
Shortcut What it does
Ctrl + K, Ctrl + O Open a folder
Ctrl + E, Ctrl + E Run the selected query (SQLTools)
Shift + Home / Shift + ↑ Select from the cursor to the line start / one more line up
Ctrl + / Turn the selected lines into comments (--) and back
Ctrl + S Save
Ctrl + Shift + P Command Palette: type any command, e.g. SQLTools: Show Table Records
Ctrl + Z Undo

Sa simpleng salita: SELECT = "show me these columns". FROM = "from this table". It's like telling the store helper: "Show me the names and prices, from the product list."

SELECT * FROM branches;                                 -- * means every column
SELECT product_name, category, unit_price FROM products;   -- only these 3 columns, in this order

Rules for writing SQL

  • End every query with ;.
  • Keywords (SELECT, FROM) can be upper or lower case. We write them in CAPITALS so they are easy to see.
  • Column names are separated by commas. No comma after the last column.
  • Text values go inside single quotes: 'GCash'. Numbers do not: 60.
  • A line starting with -- is a comment: notes for humans that the database ignores.

DISTINCT: each value only once

Sa simpleng salita: DISTINCT removes repeats. 500 sales have only 4 payment methods. DISTINCT shows each method once.

SELECT DISTINCT category FROM products;      -- 12 categories, each once

Sa simpleng salita: WHERE = "only the rows that pass this test". Like a sieve (salaan): only the rows that match fall through.

SELECT product_name, unit_price
FROM products
WHERE category = 'Beverages';
Operator Meaning Example
= equal to WHERE branch_id = 'BR03'
<> (or !=) not equal to WHERE payment_method <> 'Cash'
> < >= <= greater / less than (or equal) WHERE unit_price > 60
AND both conditions must be true WHERE branch_id = 'BR03' AND payment_method = 'GCash'
OR at least one must be true WHERE category = 'Dairy' OR category = 'Bakery'
IN (…) equal to any value in a list (short for many ORs) WHERE payment_method IN ('GCash', 'Maya')
BETWEEN a AND b from a to b, including both ends WHERE sale_date BETWEEN '2026-02-01' AND '2026-02-07'
LIKE matches a text pattern. % = any characters, _ = exactly one character WHERE product_name LIKE '%Milk%'
IS NULL / IS NOT NULL has no value / has a value WHERE email IS NULL

Watch out! - Dates are stored as text in the form YYYY-MM-DD ('2026-02-14'), so they sort and compare correctly. - Never write = NULL. It never matches anything. Always write IS NULL. - Text inside quotes must match exactly: 'Gcash' is not 'GCash'. (In SQLite, LIKE ignores upper/lower case, but = does not.) - AND before OR: WHERE a OR b AND c means a OR (b AND c). Use parentheses to be clear.

lesson.h: Part 6 — ORDER BY and LIMIT: Sort and Shorten
lesson.html:
Sa simpleng salita: ORDER BY = "arrange the rows": smallest to biggest (ASC, the default) or biggest to smallest (DESC). LIMIT 5 = "only the first 5 rows". Together they answer "top 5" questions.

-- the 5 most expensive products
SELECT product_name, unit_price
FROM products
ORDER BY unit_price DESC
LIMIT 5;
product_name unit_price
Rice - Well-milled (5 kg) 245.0
Spam Classic 340g 210.0
Cooking Oil 1L 110.0
Load - Globe/Smart P100 100.0
Eggs (1 dozen) 96.0
  • Sort by two columns: ORDER BY total_amount DESC, sale_id. The second column breaks ties.
  • The order of the clauses is fixed:
SELECT  columns        -- 1. what to show
FROM    table          -- 2. where from
WHERE   condition      -- 3. which rows
ORDER BY column        -- 4. in what order
LIMIT   n;             -- 5. how many

Memory aid: Sana Friday Will Open Late. SELECT · FROM · WHERE · ORDER BY · LIMIT.

lesson.h: Part 7 — From Business Question to Query
lesson.html:
Turn Aling Nena's question into SQL step by step:

"Which Pasig sales were paid with GCash? I need the receipt number, date and amount."

Step Ask yourself Answer
1 Which table? sales
2 Which columns to show? sale_id, sale_date, total_amount
3 Which rows (conditions)? Pasig = branch_id = 'BR03' AND payment_method = 'GCash'
4 Any order or limit? Not asked 
SELECT sale_id, sale_date, total_amount
FROM sales
WHERE branch_id = 'BR03' AND payment_method = 'GCash';

Result: 46 rows. Always read the row count and ask: does this number make sense?

Common errors and how to fix them

Message / symptom Likely cause Fix
no such table: product Table name misspelled It is products (check the SQLTools tree)
no such column: price Column name misspelled It is unit_price
near "FROM": syntax error Extra comma before FROM, or a missing comma between columns SELECT a, b FROM …
unrecognized token A quote was opened but not closed 'GCash' needs both quotes
0 rows, no error Text does not match exactly, or = NULL Check spelling/case; use IS NULL
Nothing happens Query not selected, or not connected Select it; check the status bar shows Aling Nena

Clause / keyword Purpose Example
SELECT … FROM … Show columns from a table SELECT * FROM products;
DISTINCT Remove repeated rows SELECT DISTINCT category FROM products;
WHERE Keep only rows that match WHERE unit_price > 60
AND / OR / IN Combine conditions WHERE payment_method IN ('GCash','Maya') AND quantity >= 3
BETWEEN A range, both ends included WHERE sale_date BETWEEN '2026-02-01' AND '2026-02-07'
LIKE Text pattern WHERE product_name LIKE '%Milk%'
IS NULL No value WHERE email IS NULL
ORDER BY … DESC Sort, biggest first ORDER BY unit_price DESC
LIMIT First n rows LIMIT 5
-- Comment -- Q1: all branches

Term Formal definition Sa simpleng salita
Data source The origin from which data is obtained Kung saan galing ang data
Internal / external data Data created inside the business / obtained from outside it Sariling data ng tindahan / galing sa labas
Structured data Data organized in a fixed schema of rows and columns Maayos na naka-table
Semi-structured data Data with tags or labels but no fixed table (JSON, XML) May label, pero hindi table
Unstructured data Data with no predefined format (images, audio, free text) Walang ayos: litrato, boses, comments
Database An organized collection of data stored electronically Maayos na lalagyan ng data
Relational database A database of tables linked by keys Mga table na magkakakonekta
Table / row / column A set of records / one record / one attribute Drawer / isang item / isang katangian
Primary key (PK) Column(s) that uniquely identify each row ID ng bawat row, walang kapareho
Foreign key (FK) Column that refers to a primary key in another table Turo sa ID ng ibang table
NULL The absence of a value Walang laman, hindi zero
DBMS Software that manages a database (SQLite, MySQL) Ang program na nag-aalaga ng database
SQL Structured Query Language, the standard language for relational databases Wika para magtanong sa database
Query A request for data written in SQL Tanong sa database
Result set The rows and columns a query returns Ang sagot na table
Clause A part of a SQL statement (SELECT, WHERE, …) Bahagi ng query

• Know your source first: internal or external, structured or not, who owns it, how good it is.
  • A relational database stores each thing once, in its own table, linked by keys.
  • SELECT picks columns; WHERE picks rows; ORDER BY sorts; LIMIT shortens; DISTINCT removes repeats.
  • Text in 'single quotes', dates as 'YYYY-MM-DD', and IS NULL, never = NULL.
  • Always read the row count and ask whether it makes sense.

Next session (Day 5): Extract and Combine Data · COUNT, SUM and AVG, aliases, JOINs, and exporting a query result to Excel.

labTips: Type your query in the box under each question, then tap Run to see the result. Check runs every query again and marks it.
The word buttons (SELECT, FROM, WHERE…) type for you. Tap Tables to see every table and column; tap a name to insert it.
Any correct query passes: what counts is the RESULT (the same rows and values), not the exact spelling.
Every query runs on a fresh copy of the database, so you cannot break anything. Experiment!
Tap Check to see which answers are correct, then Submit to send your work to the trainer.
